chunks: And he illustrated with the verse of a poet:
O ‘Amr! By your good father’s life. I have received only a small bit of fat from this pot (fat that remains sticking to it after it has been emptied).
ai.seo_question: What does the poetic verse 'La amru abeek al-khair' mean in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs this poetic verse to highlight the disparity in power and resource distribution during the conflict with Muawiya, where his loyalists received a modest share while the opposing faction secured the majority. This metaphor underscores the strategic reality of the Battle of Siffin and the subsequent arbitration, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the limitations of Ali's authority despite his legitimacy. The verse serves as a poignant commentary on the political fragmentation of the early Muslim community.
